capability: 2-D exterior Laplace operator: potential AND velocity field outside a body, plus the prescribed-circulation (rotating cylinder) exterior Neumann problem, verified against the cylinder complex potential

reference.velocity: dW/dz = u - i v = U (1 - a**2/z**2)
reference.perturbation_potential: phi - U x = U a**2 cos(theta) / r
reference.lifting_complex_potential: W(z) = U (z + a**2/z) - i Gamma/(2 pi) ln(z/a) (Gamma counter-clockwise)
reference.lifting_velocity: dW/dz = u - i v = U (1 - a**2/z**2) - i Gamma/(2 pi z)
reference.lifting_surface_speed: v_theta = Gamma/(2 pi a) - 2 U sin(theta); Cp = 1 - (v_theta/U)**2
bibliography: Lamb H. Hydrodynamics. 6th ed. Cambridge University Press, 1932: uniform flow past a circular cylinder (same edition as docs/classical_benchmarks.md ref. [1]).
Milne-Thomson L M. Theoretical Hydrodynamics. 5th ed. Macmillan, 1968: circle theorem / translating-cylinder potential (docs/classical_benchmarks.md ref. [3]).
reference.page_or_article_number: WITHHELD: neither book is reachable from this container, so the exact page/article number was not verified here; the formulas are elementary and are instead re-derived numerically by the harmonicity gate (Laplacian and curl of the reference).

dirichlet.boundary_data: phi' = U a**2 cos(theta)/r on panel midpoints
dirichlet.recovered: potential and grad(phi) at exterior probes

neumann.boundary_data: q_e = U a**2 cos(theta)/r**2 (zero total normal velocity)
neumann.recovered: surface velocity from q_e and d(phi)/ds; grad(phi) outside

declared.surface_speed: v_theta = Gamma/(2 pi a) - 2 U sin(theta)
declared.imposed: doublet Neumann data q_e = grad(phi_d).n_e plus the unit-vortex response q_e = v_unit.n_body; the circulation itself is prescribed, so no Kutta condition is solved
declared.recovered: surface velocity from the solved traces, pressure integral for lift and drag, interpolated zeros of v_theta for the stagnation points

floor.note: the case acceptance is < 3 % on the exterior velocity field; this block measures *where* that holds. Above the reported clearance the worst-direction relative error is inside the tolerance, below it the field is outside the acceptance however many criteria pass -- the probe rings of routes D/N stop at r/a = 1.25, i.e. delta = 0.25 a, which is many panels out on every level, so the routes themselves are unaffected

azimuth.probe_directions: along one panel from the midpoint to the vertex (bisector normal at the vertex), pushed out along the local outward normal
azimuth.note: zones are reported per azimuth: the midpoint column reproduces the radial ladder (from the circle, so it agrees to a few percent) while the worst column is the honest bound for an arbitrary target

midpoint_cross_check.note: the radial ladder probes at radius a + delta (measured from the circle) and the azimuthal sweep at chord midpoint + delta (measured from the polygon), so the same midpoint direction differs by the faceting offset; agreement within NEAR_WALL_AZIMUTH_FRAME_TOL confirms both studies measure the same regime

faceting.note: probes measured from the inscribed polygon surface rather than from the circle: the residual difference is the faceting offset a(1-cos(pi/N)) ~ h^2/8, which is O(h) relative to delta = 0.1 h_max and is the reason the exclusion-zone error saturates at first order instead of improving like h^2

linear.note: linear_density=True expands both panel densities as sigma(s) = sigma_i + sigma'_i (s - L_i/2) with closed-form first-moment integrals.  On the finest level its 1%-accurate window moves in from delta = 2 h_max to delta = 0.5 h_max, but the coarse levels do not follow: the worst-over-levels window is 2 h_max, the same as constant panels.  The gain is therefore a finest-mesh statement, not a widened envelope

attribution.note: the two representation rows use the exact traces at the panel midpoints, so they isolate the panel basis from the solve; the difference between them and the sweep rows above measures how much of the near-wall error is boundary-trace error amplified as 1/delta

near_wall.probe_directions: radial, one above each panel midpoint
near_wall.note: the error reported here is the total velocity (grad(phi) + U x_hat) against dW/dz at the same points; it is a property of the constant-density panel representation, not of the linear solver

uniform_flow.contaminants: A_2 = A_3 = A_4 = 0 and no 2-D source
uniform_flow.bibliography: Lamb H. Hydrodynamics, 6th ed., 1932 (uniform flow past a cylinder).

pure_strain.excitation: plane straining flow u = gamma x, v = -gamma y
pure_strain.contaminants: A_1 = A_3 = A_4 = 0 and no 2-D source
pure_strain.bibliography: Milne-Thomson L M. Theoretical Hydrodynamics, 5th ed., 1968: straining flow past a circular cylinder.

mirror_split.note: the axis-aligned body/data/probe set are mirror-symmetric about y = 0, so a mirror-symmetric implementation leaves only the even part; the oblique headings are the ones that would expose a y-odd defect

heading_sweep.note: the lattice level rotates body and probes together by 90 deg (a whole number of panel steps with an exact rotation matrix), so it must reproduce the axis-aligned solve to roundoff; the half-panel and 30 deg headings break the mirror symmetry of the axis-aligned configuration while leaving the body in place

criteria.name: geometry_vertices_on_circle
criteria.note: the body must be the inscribed polygon of radius a, not a rescaled one

criteria.name: geometry_area_matches_inscribed_closed_form
criteria.note: polygon area vs N/2 a^2 sin(2 pi/N)

criteria.name: geometry_perimeter_matches_inscribed_closed_form
criteria.note: polygon perimeter vs 2 N a sin(pi/N)

criteria.name: reference_is_harmonic
criteria.note: Laplacian of the closed-form perturbation potential at the probes

criteria.name: reference_is_irrotational
criteria.note: curl of the closed-form velocity at the probes

criteria.name: field_gradient_matches_finite_difference
criteria.note: closed-form panel-integral gradients vs central differences of the potential

criteria.name: dirichlet_velocity_relative_l2
criteria.note: BEM grad(phi) + U x_hat vs dW/dz at the exterior probes (budget panels)

criteria.name: dirichlet_potential_relative_l2
criteria.note: recovered perturbation potential vs closed form (same probes)

criteria.name: neumann_surface_velocity_relative_l2
criteria.note: fluid-side surface velocity vs 2 U sin(theta) at the panel midpoints

criteria.name: neumann_velocity_relative_l2
criteria.note: BEM grad(phi) + U x_hat vs dW/dz at the exterior probes

criteria.name: neumann_normal_velocity_residual
criteria.note: the body must be a streamline (max |v.n|/U)

criteria.name: neumann_cp_relative_l2
criteria.note: Cp = 1 - (|v|/U)^2 vs 1 - 4 sin^2(theta) at the panel midpoints

criteria.name: neumann_surface_velocity_observed_order
criteria.note: second-order faceting convergence of the polygon surface velocity

criteria.name: near_wall_window_error
criteria.note: at the documented clearance window delta = 2 h_max the exterior velocity error stays inside one third of the case tolerance, on every ladder level

criteria.name: near_wall_window_error_scales_with_h
criteria.note: the window error is a discretisation error: it must shrink as h shrinks (first order at best; the constant-density term dominates)

criteria.name: near_wall_exclusion_zone_is_real
criteria.note: inside delta = 0.1 h_max the constant-panel field is *not* usable; documenting the window only means something if this holds

criteria.name: near_wall_error_is_panel_relative
criteria.note: at fixed delta/h_max mesh refinement must not buy near-wall accuracy (ratio of the error at the coarsest and the finest level)

criteria.name: near_wall_guard_rejects_inside_window
criteria.note: minimum_clearance_factor must refuse targets closer than the requested clearance instead of returning a plausible wrong velocity

criteria.name: near_wall_tolerance_boundary_is_located
criteria.note: the acceptance is < 3 % on the exterior velocity field, so the record must say *where* that holds: on every level the worst-direction error has to cross the tolerance inside the probed clearance grid, otherwise the usable region is unbounded (an assumed bound) or empty

criteria.name: near_wall_tolerance_boundary_moves_inward_with_refinement
criteria.note: refining the mesh may not shrink the usable envelope: if the boundary moved outward the reported window would be a property of one mesh only

criteria.name: near_wall_window_clears_measured_tolerance_boundary
criteria.note: the gated 1 % window delta = 2 h_max must sit at least 2x outside the *measured* 3 % boundary, so the acceptance is not true merely because the window was placed next to the edge of the region where it fails

criteria.name: near_wall_linear_window_extends_the_finest_window
criteria.note: on the finest level the first-moment (linear density) basis must hold the 1 % bound at delta = 0.5 h_max, against 2 h_max for constant panels.  This is the measurement the original single criterion quoted -- and it only holds there; see the worst-case criterion below

criteria.name: near_wall_linear_window_does_not_widen_the_worst_case_window
criteria.note: the 1 % window of the first-moment basis over *all* levels may not be advertised as wider than the constant-panel window.  A previous revision asserted delta = 0.5 h_max here; measurement falsified it (on N = 32 the linear error is 1.579e-02 at delta = 1 h_max and 1.639e-02 at 0.5 h_max, i.e. outside 1 %), so the level-independent part of that claim is retired while the finest-level part is kept in near_wall_linear_window_extends_the_finest_window.  Recorded in docs/CASE-BEM-LAPLACE-CYLINDER-NEAR-WALL-CRITERIA-AUDIT.md

criteria.name: near_wall_linear_beats_constant_basis
criteria.note: at delta = 0.5 h_max the linear-density error must be at least three times smaller than the constant-density error on the finest level

criteria.name: near_wall_exclusion_floor_is_faceting
criteria.threshold: surface_referenced > circle_referenced on every level and (amplification - 1)/(offset/delta) in [0.3, 1.2], decaying with h
criteria.note: the exclusion-zone floor is geometric faceting: the inscribed polygon's panel midpoints sit at a(1-cos(pi/N)) ~ h^2/8 below the circle, an O(h) offset relative to delta = 0.1 h_max, so a probe re-referenced to the polygon surface is the same offset *closer* to the density it integrates and its error must *grow* -- the earlier 'must collapse by 3x' phrasing had the sign of the geometry inverted (measured 1.04x the other way, cj3969).  What faceting explains is the growth *rate*: the amplification per unit offset is level independent (0.69 / 0.61 / 0.59 from coarse to fine) and the amplification itself decays with h, which is the O(h) claim this criterion now measures

criteria.name: near_wall_window_is_azimuth_independent
criteria.note: the documented window was measured above the panel midpoints only; walking the probe across the panel (midpoint -> vertex) must not break the same 1% tolerance, otherwise the window is an azimuth-specific statement rather than a validity claim

criteria.name: near_wall_exclusion_is_worse_at_vertices
criteria.note: inside the exclusion zone the midpoint column is the *best* azimuth: at the vertex the piecewise-constant density is discontinuous across the kink, so the quoted midpoint number understates the worst case

criteria.name: near_wall_azimuth_window_is_not_extended_by_linear_density
criteria.note: the midpoint-only study moves the 1% window of the first-moment basis in to 0.5 h_max; once the azimuth is free that gain disappears, so the linear basis must not be advertised as widening the usable window

criteria.name: near_wall_linear_density_is_worse_in_the_window
criteria.note: inside the documented window the first-moment basis is measurably worse than constant panels (its arc-length slope extrapolates the density across the vertex), which is the qualification the library docstring needs

criteria.name: near_wall_azimuth_midpoint_cross_check
criteria.note: the azimuthal sweep and the radial ladder probe the same midpoint direction from different reference surfaces (chord vs circle); their agreement is what makes the two windows comparable

criteria.name: multipole_uniform_flow_moment_relative_error
criteria.note: far-field harmonic A_1 recovered from the ring fits vs A_1 = U a**2 (budget panels)

criteria.name: multipole_uniform_flow_moment_observed_order
criteria.note: the faceting error of the multipole moment must converge with h

criteria.name: multipole_pure_strain_moment_relative_error
criteria.note: far-field harmonic A_2 recovered from the ring fits vs A_2 = (gamma/2) a**4 (budget panels)

criteria.name: multipole_pure_strain_moment_observed_order
criteria.note: the faceting error of the multipole moment must converge with h

criteria.name: multipole_purity
criteria.note: harmonics the boundary data does not excite must stay at roundoff (largest spurious A_n over the moment scale, every level)

criteria.name: multipole_no_source_leak
criteria.note: the exterior field must be solenoidal: no 2-D log source, measured as the slope of the ring mean against log(r)

criteria.name: multipole_radius_independence
criteria.note: the moment measured on r/a = 1.5, 2.5, 4 must not depend on the ring

criteria.name: multipole_fit_residual
criteria.note: the truncated harmonic fit must explain the sampled field (relative rms residual of the order-4 fit)

criteria.name: multipole_mirror_control_is_rejected
criteria.note: the image-sign data must be read as a negative dipole, i.e. the moment carries its sign

criteria.name: circulation_surface_velocity_relative_l2
criteria.note: surface speed vs v_theta = Gamma/(2 pi a) - 2 U sin(theta) at the budget mesh

criteria.name: circulation_cp_relative_l2
criteria.note: Cp built from the same surface velocity that is integrated for the lift

criteria.name: circulation_velocity_relative_l2
criteria.note: external velocity field vs dW/dz of the lifting complex potential

criteria.name: circulation_measured_matches_prescribed
criteria.note: the counter-clockwise contour integral of the solved surface velocity must reproduce the prescribed Gamma, otherwise the lift agreement is a coincidence

criteria.name: circulation_lift_matches_joukowski
criteria.note: pressure-integrated lift vs L' = -rho U Gamma

criteria.name: circulation_drag_vanishes
criteria.note: d'Alembert: no drag in a steady inviscid flow, for any Gamma

criteria.name: circulation_stagnation_angle_matches_closed_form
criteria.note: interpolated zeros of the surface tangential velocity vs sin(theta_s) = Gamma/(4 pi U a)

criteria.name: circulation_observed_order
criteria.note: the circulation route must converge on refinement (faceting O(h^2)) instead of sitting at a plateau

criteria.name: circulation_sweep_lift_is_linear
criteria.note: lift/(rho U Gamma) must stay at 1 across Gamma in (1.0, 2.0, 3.0)

criteria.name: wrong_reference_is_rejected
criteria.note: the mirrored image-sign flow must not be accepted by the reference

criteria.name: far_field_matches_closed_form
criteria.note: at r = 8a (disturbance still ~3% of U) the BEM velocity matches dW/dz to 1% of U

criteria.name: oblique_heading_dirichlet_velocity
criteria.note: rotating the body against the inflow breaks the mirror symmetry about the flow axis; worst heading 0 deg

criteria.name: oblique_heading_neumann_surface_velocity
criteria.note: route N surface velocity with the stagnation streamline over a chord midpoint instead of a vertex; worst heading 1.40625 deg

criteria.name: oblique_heading_within_penalty_of_axis
criteria.note: an oblique heading must not be materially worse than the axis-aligned one

criteria.name: mirror_antisymmetric_error_is_roundoff
criteria.note: the axis-aligned body, data and probe set are mirror-symmetric about y = 0; an antisymmetric residual would mean the implementation, not the configuration, introduced the asymmetry (and could have cancelled)

criteria.name: lattice_heading_is_covariant
criteria.note: 32 panel steps rotate the body onto itself, so the recovered velocity field must not move
